content:
miguel (support): FYI customer aiapp-prod reporting ~40% 503s on /v1/generate since 04:12 UTC. Errors show upstream 500 and sudden runner exits. attaching brief logs below.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0473, severity: high. Pager duty notified.

miguel (support): logs: 
```
[04:12:34] runner-quickline-prod-3: segfault at 0x7f... ip=0x4012f4
[04:12:34] runtime: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: failed to allocate 4096MB
[04:12:35] process exited with signal SIGBUS (code=0x1)
[04:12:35] coredump: /var/crash/infer-runner.12345.dmp
```

anna (sre): Thanks. Do we have QPS / concurrency during spike and node kernel/driver versions? Any recent infra changes?

miguel (support): Customer provided payload: high QPS (~220 rps) with concurrency=8 and avg seq length=1800 after system prompt. They rolled a model variant 2 hours ago. No infra changes reported on their side.

joel (eng-runtime): Noted. On our side there was a staged nvidia-driver roll on that cluster at 02:30 UTC (driver 525 -> 535) and a runtime kernel patch 02:45. We didn't flag for all pools; might have hit this worker. Also see recent prefetch kv optimization merged yesterday.

maria (support): Repro steps from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-70b","concurrency":8,"inputs":[{"prompt":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":2048}]}'
```

anna (sre): Immediate mitigation: route affected traffic away from pool quickline-prod to fallback pool t2-stable, reduce target concurrency to 2, and disable kv-prefetch on-host for now. maria can you apply?

maria (support): Done. Routing policy updated at 04:20 UTC -> fallback t2-stable. Concurrency cap applied. Monitoring: error rate dropped from 40% -> 1.8% within 90s. Customer confirms degraded but functional. :white_check_mark: 

joel (eng-runtime): Thanks. We need minidump + full coredump diff. anna, can you capture /var/crash from that host and check dmesg for kernel OOM vs GPU driver fault? I suspect the driver upgrade + aggressive prefetch caused memory fragmentation and then SIGBUS during pointer deref.

anna (sre): Collecting crash bundle now. dmesg shows "NVRM: GPU at X: GPU has fallen off the bus" and repeated CUDA OOM messages. Also seeing "ELF: bad relocation" in the process log around same time. Uploading to /tmp/INC-2026-0473/bundle.tar.gz

joel (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) eng-runtime to analyze coredump and verify whether regression introduced by prefetch commit (PR #486). 2) eng-sre to roll back driver to 525 on affected pool and repro under load. 3) support to keep fallback routing and coordinate with customer for controlled repro window. I'll take (1).

maria (support): Customer asked for ETA. I've offered a controlled repro window in 2 hours; they agreed to low-traffic test. Keeping them on fallback until we confirm stable.

anna (sre): Short-term config tweaks we applied: ulimit -l increase, disabled mmap hugepages for runner, and set environment var REDWOOD_PREFETCH_KV=false on quickline nodes (we toggled the flag before fully rolling out). If rollback confirms driver issue we'll schedule a canary re-roll.

joel (eng-runtime): I'll grep the coredump for allocation pattern and check whether the address space was corrupted (heap/stack overflow vs kernel driver fault). If it's prefetch, revert PR and run our loadbench with seq len 1800, concurrency 8.

miguel (support): Noted. Customer impact reduced, keeping on the thread. Will update customer with mitigation steps and next repro window.

anna (sre): Assigning owners: eng-runtime/joel -> investigate coredump + PR review; eng-sre -> driver rollback verification. Leaving incident open. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0473

maria (support): tagging customer contact: @alice (aiapp-prod) — thank you for patience. We'll follow up after the repro.

miguel (support): Closing loop for now, will reopen if errors recur after next deploy. Incident remains with eng teams for root cause.
